summary: Frontend-only verification of the new ThinkingLoader (infinity-loop) inline indicator replacing the Loader2 spinner. Live login as test@aurem.dev on preview, sent chat message, and verified: (1) ThinkingLoader renders inside data-testid=chat-thinking with NO Lucide Loader2 inside; (2) 3-dot typing-indicator (aria-label='ORA is thinking') is still rendered above (regression preserved); (3) particle position visibly changes between two ~500ms-apart samples (animation actively running, not frozen); (4) useId-generated filter ids are unique per instance; (5) forcing document.documentElement[data-theme]='light' and sending a second message causes the loader's data-theme-variant attribute to flip to 'light' (MutationObserver wiring works in the live React app); (6) no pageerrors thrown, no duplicate-id / SVG warnings in the console. Screenshot artifacts saved for dark + light. LoopLiveFeed pending-tone swap was verified via static code inspection only (import + `style.spin && !isStalled ? <ThinkingLoader/> : <Icon>` block confirmed at LoopLiveFeed.jsx:683-684) — not exercised live because no pending narration line was active during the smoke chat send.
critical_code_review_comments: ThinkingLoader.jsx is clean, self-contained, uses useId() for unique filter/path ids, and the MutationObserver on document.documentElement[data-theme] disconnects on unmount — no leaks.

One tiny nit: the JSDoc example says '<ThinkingLoader size={36} /> // still single-particle' but the actual threshold SINGLE_PARTICLE_BELOW=28 means size=36 renders DUAL, not single. Comment is misleading but not a functional bug.

LoopLiveFeed leaves the old narration-spin CSS animation as dead-but-harmless code for the stalled/static case as stated — acceptable, but a follow-up cleanup pass could remove the unused CSS keyframes to shrink the bundle.

Cookie banner intercepts clicks in the preview — dismiss with 'Reject non-essential' before interacting. Monaco code editor on the dashboard also has a hidden .ime-text-area textarea that first matches generic 'textarea' selectors; use `textarea[placeholder*="Ask ORA"]` to target the real chat input.
